subject: Capacity sizing options + soft rollback pathway for NovusEnt dedicated reservation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan@novusent.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity sizing options + soft rollback pathway for NovusEnt dedicated reservation

Jordan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a concise options sheet that maps a few reservation configurations to the expected NovusEnt traffic profile you shared. High level:

- Scenario A (Conservative baseline): 40 GPUs reserved (min 36 active) — phased activation over 8 weeks. Best for steady-state predictability and lowest risk of throttling.
- Scenario B (Elastic baseline + buffer): 60 GPUs reserved (min 48 active) — 4-week ramp to handle peak launches, includes 20% burst credit for spikes.
- Scenario C (Fast-launch ramp): 80 GPUs reserved (min 60 active) — 2-week aggressive ramp for product launch windows, higher cost but lower throttling SLOs.

Recommendations and safety / rollback language: we propose a soft rollback clause during the first 90 days that allows NovusEnt to step down committed minimums by up to one tranche (e.g., reduce min active by 20%) with 30 days notice, provided observed utilization is below agreed thresholds. This gives you flexibility if usage growth is slower than forecast without immediate decommit penalties.

I've attached the demand profile (Novus_Demand_Profile.xlsx) and a draft SLA with redlines we typically include (Draft_SLA_redlines.pdf). Please review the ramp/cost tradeoffs and let us know which scenario you want priced with firm monthly/annual commit mixes.

Next steps: if you confirm Scenario B (likely fit for launch + runway), Karthik can share a formal commercial term sheet and we can add language for the 90-day soft rollback to the SOW.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Deal Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachments: Novus_Demand_Profile.xlsx (spreadsheet), Draft_SLA_redlines.pdf (pdf)
From: Jordan Myers <jordan@novusent.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity sizing options + soft rollback pathway for NovusEnt dedicated reservation

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear options. A few follow-ups from product and procurement:

1) Can you surface the expected P50/P95 token latency and throughput per GPU for each scenario? We need to be sure Scenario B meets our launch SLOs.
2) The 90-day soft rollback is interesting — procurement asked whether the rollback is limited to minimum active GPUs only or if it can apply to committed reserved capacity (and what the pricing implications would be).
3) For Scenario C, what is the warmup plan (how many pre-warmed pods / hours) do you recommend to avoid cold-cache latency spikes on day 1 of a launch?

Procurement: adding you on thread. We'll need a clear definition of the utilization thresholds that trigger a permitted rollback and the financial treatment of any retro changes.

Jordan
VP Product, Novus Enterprise
jordan@novusent.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing sketch + rollback mechanics for NOVUS-2027-042

Internal note (do not send):

Marissa / Grace —

Sketch of numbers to respond with:
- Scenario A: $Xk/month reserved (40 GPUs) — effective per-GPU token cost baseline. Min-active pricing applies at 90% of reserve (standard).
- Scenario B (recommended): $Yk/month reserved (60 GPUs) with 20% burst credit; include a 90-day soft rollback allowance that reduces min-active by up to 20% without early termination fee; any further decommits -> standard decommit schedule.
- Scenario C: $Zk/month (80 GPUs) — include a warmup plan: 48 hours of pre-warmed lanes, progressive KV-cache priming, and a 7-day elevated throughput window (credits apply).

Rollback mechanics (legal-friendly wording): allow one-time soft reduction of min-active values within the first 90 days, subject to 30-day notice and a utilization audit (we'll use average capacity utilization < 35% across a 21-day window as the trigger). If utilization rebounds above the threshold within 60 days, the customer returns to the prior min-active level or pays the delta retro for that period.

Attachments to include in reply: demand profile, performance appendix (P50/P95 per GPU), example SOW clause.

I'll draft a short addendum for procurement to sign off on and loop legal if Novus pushes for rollback on reserved capacity rather than only min-active.

-karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan@novusent.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novusent.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity sizing options + soft rollback pathway for NovusEnt dedicated reservation

Jordan / Procurement team —

Thanks for the questions. Quick responses inline below and attached a short Performance Appendix with P50/P95 throughput/latency per GPU for the model family you plan to serve.

1) Latency/throughput: attached appendix shows expected P50 token latency of ~25ms and P95 ~90ms for the small-medium request distribution at 1k-token sequences on the benchmarked instance we recommend. Scenario C reduces end-to-end P95 by ~12% due to added headroom.

2) Rollback scope: our legal-commercial preference is to limit the soft rollback to the committed min-active floor (operational minimums that drive provisioning) rather than the full reserved capacity. The reason: reserved capacity determines inventory planning beyond short notice windows; allowing rollback on full reserved amounts materially impacts our capacity commitments. That said, we can consider a narrowly scoped rollback on reserved capacity if you accept a graduated fee (e.g., a proportional early reduction credit schedule). We will capture both options in the term sheet for you to choose.

3) Warmup for Scenario C: recommended 48–72 hours of pre-warmed lanes and a KV cache priming plan. We'll include a one-time warmup credit to offset incremental burn during launch if you select Scenario C.

Next steps:
- If you confirm Scenario B, I'll send a commercial term sheet with two rollback variants (min-active-only vs. reserved-reduction-with-fee).
- If procurement prefers reserved rollback as the default, flag now and we'll engage legal to outline the proportional fee schedule.

Attached: Performance_Appendix.pdf, Updated_Term_Sheet_Draft.docx, Novus_Demand_Profile.xlsx

Best —
Marissa
Sr. Deal Lead, Redwood Inference
